=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text pw "popcount of 3^0 .. 3^29:"
text evil "first 30 evil numbers:  "
text odious "first 30 odious numbers:"
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note Kernighan: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit
fn popc n ulong to ulong
c = ulong 0
v = n
while gt v 0 bound 64
v = and v sub v 1
c = add c 1
end
ret c
end
note evil numbers have an even population count, odious ones an odd count
fn list want ulong to void
c = ulong 0
n = ulong 0
while lt c 30 bound 100
if eq rem popc n 2 want
emit sp
emitu n
c = add c 1
end
n = add n 1
end
emit nl
end
fn main to int
emit pw
p = ulong 1
for i ulong 30
emit sp
emitu popc p
p = mul p 3
end
emit nl
emit evil
list 0
emit odious
list 1
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
popcount of 3^0 .. 3^29: 1 2 2 4 3 6 6 5 6 8 9 13 10 11 14 15 11 14 14 17 17 20 19 22 16 18 24 30 25 25
first 30 evil numbers:   0 3 5 6 9 10 12 15 17 18 20 23 24 27 29 30 33 34 36 39 40 43 45 46 48 51 53 54 57 58
first 30 odious numbers: 1 2 4 7 8 11 13 14 16 19 21 22 25 26 28 31 32 35 37 38 41 42 44 47 49 50 52 55 56 59
</pre>
